summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with a history of chronic pancreatitis secondary to vasculitis and prior distal pancreatectomy, was admitted for acute abdominal pain, nausea, and gray stools. Labs showed normal amylase and lipase, and ultrasound ruled out cholecystitis. She was treated with IV fluids, bowel rest, antiemetics, and narcotic pain control, with gradual improvement. Her diet was advanced successfully, and she remained stable. A urinary tract infection was diagnosed based on new dysuria and urinalysis findings, prompting a short course of ciprofloxacin. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to continue her baseline medications, complete the antibiotic course, and follow up with her primary care provider if urinary symptoms persisted.
problems: Urinary tract infection, site not specified
